bug_semantics: phpMyFAQ's PDF export (Export/Pdf/Wrapper extends TCPDF) overrides Image() and, for any non-data, non-@ image src, reads the referenced file from disk: urldecode + concatenatePaths resolve the path under PMF_ROOT_DIR, file_get_contents slurps it, and when the bytes are not a valid image checkBase64Image() calls imagecreatefromstring() which emits a PHP warning/E_WARNING that surfaces as an uncaught exception whose stack trace (via TCPDF error handling) discloses part of the file's contents (e.g. content/core/config/database.php read via an in an FAQ answer; truncated by zend.exception_string_param_max_len by default). A user with FAQ-edit permission can thus exfiltrate local files under the web root through PDF export (CWE-200/CWE-209 information exposure through error message).
flaw_origin: Commit 06df60e776115aaeaeb99397330786cb89fcae63 ("fix: avoid image display errors in PDF due to SSL verification and caching issues", 2024-11-08, author+committer Thorsten Rinne) rewrote the Wrapper::Image override to read EVERY resolved image path from disk — `$data = file_get_contents(PMF_ROOT_DIR . $file)` — before checking `checkBase64Image($data)`, i.e. imagecreatefromstring() on arbitrary local file bytes. This converted the image handler into the file-read + warning-exception primitive the advisory exploits; parent b1d25c3bf7 only decoded data: URIs and never read arbitrary local paths (the file: branch did not exist). The advisory's named sink (uncaught warning-exception disclosing non-image local file contents during PDF generation) is born at this commit; the later refinement 46436ed7c8a (2024-11-14, concatenatePaths with content/ substring anchoring) still read arbitrary content/-anchored files, and e9b97a24af1 (2026-06-06, #4327) added is_file/is_readable checks without any image-content validation, so the disclosure primitive persisted until 7a82e3ff591.
ai_marker: decomposed-wave marker only — b097f61004d8103e14c694fb727998ae440fa265 (2025-08-03, urldecode of image filenames, part of the file-read pipeline the disclosure flows through) is authored by copilot-swe-agent[bot] with 'Co-authored-by: thorsten'; the BIC 06df60e77611 itself carries no AI marker (grep NONE sentinel). Per BIC-only attribution the bot-authored wave never sets the verdict.
evidence: Advisory (CVE-2026-76210 / GHSA-m98p-5698-x2wc): phpMyFAQ before 4.1.7 does not adequately sanitize HTML in FAQ answers before generating PDFs via TCPDF; an attacker with FAQ-create/edit permission embeds an referencing a local file under content/ (e.g. content/core/config/database.php); PDF generation reads the file, the non-image bytes trigger an uncaught exception whose stack trace discloses file contents (truncated by zend.exception_string_param_max_len, larger config values disclose entire files incl. database credentials).

BIC creation check: 06df60e77611 (2024-11-08) rewrites Wrapper::Image: `$data = file_get_contents(PMF_ROOT_DIR . $file)` unconditionally, then `if ($this->checkBase64Image($data))` — checkBase64Image calls imagecreatefromstring($base64), which emits E_WARNING on non-image bytes; at parent b1d25c3bf7 the method only transformed data: URIs and passed everything else to parent::Image without any local file read.

Persistence wave (decomposed): 46436ed7c8a (2024-11-14) routed the read through concatenatePaths(PMF_ROOT_DIR, $file) with 'content' substring anchoring — still reads any path containing 'content'; e9b97a24af1 (2026-06-06, #4327) added is_file/is_readable + data:URI branch but no image-content gate; b097f61004d8 (2025-08-03, copilot-swe-agent[bot]) added urldecode($file) widening src forms; b709ebe69405 (2026-06-13, 'hardened image paths', isWithinRoot traversal guard) confined paths to the web root but STILL read non-image local files, leaving the warning-exception disclosure primitive intact.

Fix commit 7a82e3ff5917 (2026-08-01, Thorsten Rinne, 'fix: prevented local file disclosure via PDF image handler', in tag 4.1.7): inverts the flow — `if (!$this->checkBase64Image($data)) { return; }` refuses to process non-image bytes at all, and wraps imagecreatefromstring/getimagesizefromstring in set_error_handler/restore_error_handler so the E_WARNING can no longer surface as an exception; fixes 648-710 region of Wrapper.php.
Version boundary: fix 7a82e3ff5917 is an ancestor of tag 4.1.7, matching the advisory's fixed version 4.1.7; BIC 06df60e77611's read-everything design shipped from the 2024-11 line onward.

AI-marker screening: `git log --format='%an <%ae>%n%cn <%ce>%n%B' -1` on 06df60e77611, b709ebe69405, e9b97a24af1 — human-only, no AI identities (NONE sentinels); b097f61004d8 is authored by copilot-swe-agent[bot] (recorded in ai_marker, decomposed wave only).

reasoning: Vulnerability first: the advisory describes local files being read during PDF generation with non-image bytes surfacing through an uncaught exception; the code shows exactly that primitive — file_get_contents of the attacker-named path followed by imagecreatefromstring on the bytes — and the fix gates the whole path behind checkBase64Image with a warning handler, proving the unvalidated read + warning path is the defect. BIC choice: 06df60e77611 created the file-read primitive in Image() that the advisory's named sink depends on; parent had no local-file read. The read path was refined (46436ed7c8a, b097f61004d8, e9b97a24af1) and partially hardened (b709ebe69405) without removing the disclosure primitive, so squash_decomposed=true with those shas in decomposed_shas.
